fields.rationale: States cluster by what drives reciprocity eligibility: whether a formal bilateral agreement is required, whether equivalent standards alone suffice, whether a minimum years-of-experience threshold is added, whether an exam waiver is the primary mechanism with extra conditions, whether a signed written reciprocity compact is explicitly mandated, or whether the board exercises broad discretion.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must hold equivalent license from another state or territory, meet Alaska qualification standards, and have passed an equivalent examination; upon proof, the department waives the Alaska examination.
The other state must have standards of practice or licensure equal to or higher than Alabama's. The board shall actively seek to reciprocate with qualifying states.
Applicant must hold equivalent license in another state, pay required fees, submit proof of out-of-state license, and a reciprocal agreement must exist between Arkansas and that state.

Reciprocity available on a case-by-case basis if the other state accepts CA qualifications and has equivalent or higher standards; trade exam may be waived if the applicant provides written certification that their out-of-state license has been in good standing for the previous five years.

Licensure by endorsement requires substantially equivalent credentials and qualifications; licensure by reciprocity requires a reciprocal agreement with the other state's electrical board where qualifications are substantially equivalent to Colorado's.

Applicant must present proof of current licensure in good standing in another state, DC, or US territory with substantially similar standards. If standards are not substantially similar, applicant must have practiced for a minimum of 5 years after licensure.

Applicant must meet FL certification requirements and have passed a substantially equivalent exam from another jurisdiction; OR hold a valid license from another state/territory with substantially equivalent criteria; OR have held a valid license from another state/territory for at least 10 years. Must complete a 2-hour Florida Building Code course.
Other states must have requirements substantially equal to Georgia's requirements for registration, licensure, and certification, and must offer a similar privilege to Georgia residents.

Applicant must have been licensed by another state for at least one year, pay the required fee, and demonstrate qualifications equal to Iowa licensees of the same class; reciprocity only available to the extent the other state offers similar action.
Applicant must have qualifications at least equal to Idaho requirements, pay the required fee, and furnish proof thereof; no written examination required for qualifying applicants.

Licensure by endorsement available if the applicant is registered, licensed, or certified in another state with substantially equal requirements, is in good standing, and the issuing state extends similar reciprocity to Kentucky licensees.

Applicant must hold a license in a comparable classification in another state; the licensing state must provide written certification that the applicant passed the examination and is in good standing. The business law requirement shall not be waived. Applicants must comply with all other licensing requirements.
Applicant must have been licensed as an electrician in another state under laws that, in the opinion of the examiners, maintain standards substantially the same as those of Massachusetts.

Applicant must be licensed in another state/territory, have been actively engaged in electrician's work for at least 8,000 hours, and that state/territory must have equivalent licensing standards and grant similar privileges to Maine licensees. The board may waive the 576 hours of study required for journeyman or master license.

For sign specialty licensure, applicant must be licensed/registered in another state with equivalent or higher standards; board issues license without examination. For armed forces members/veterans/dependents, licensure without examination available if other state requirements substantially equivalent. Temporary licenses available to out-of-state licensees in good standing.

Applicant must hold a valid comparable license in the qualifying state, held continuously for at least one year; qualifying state must administer statewide licensing with exam and experience comparable to Minnesota; applicant must not have failed the same class of MN exam or had such license revoked/suspended; applicant must not have failed to renew for 2+ years.

Holders of a local electrical contractor or master electrician license must: provide evidence of passing a standardized written electrical assessment examination based on the NEC administered by an independent testing agency; provide evidence of 12,000 hours of verifiable practical experience or having been licensed by any Missouri political subdivision requiring examination as an electrical contractor or master electrician for 6 of the previous 8 calendar years; provide proof of insurance; and proof that the local license was current, active, and not subject to discipline.

Reciprocal recognition available where the other state's similar board recognizes Mississippi certificates. Universal recognition also available under § 73-50-2 for applicants holding a current and valid license in good standing in another state with similar scope of practice held for at least one year.

The other state's license standards must be substantially equivalent to or greater than Montana's standards, and there must be no reason to deny the license under Montana law. Applicant must affirm they have requested verification of licensure status from their other state(s).
Applicant must be licensed by another state that provides for similar reciprocal action; qualifications must be equal to NC holders; payment of required fee.
Reciprocal state must provide for licensing of electricians and similar reciprocal action; applicant must pay the required fee and prove qualifications equal to ND license holders of similar class.

Applicant must have been licensed by another state for at least one year, pay required fee, and demonstrate qualifications equal to Nebraska holders of similar licenses. Additional pathway available for reciprocal credentialing agreements, military occupational specialty, or US DOL-registered apprenticeship program completion.
Requirements or standards for certification or licensure in the other state must be equivalent to or greater than those in New Hampshire. May include examination on NH laws and payment of a fee.

Board discretion; requires equal reciprocity from the other jurisdiction for NJ licensees. Out-of-state individuals may also obtain a temporary license without examination for up to 30 days per triennial renewal period.
Reciprocal licensing agreement with any state having equivalent licensing requirements, subject to consent of the commission.

A written reciprocity agreement between Ohio and the other state must exist; the other state's requirements must be substantially equal to Ohio's; the other state must extend similar reciprocity to Ohio licensees; applicant must pay the licensure fee.

Applicant must hold a valid license issued by another governmental entity with licensing requirements similar to those in the Electrical License Act; temporary licenses available during declared disasters for out-of-state journeymen who apply for examination within 10 days of beginning work.

Reciprocal agreements available when other state's standards, qualifications and examinations are substantially similar to Oregon's; license issued without examination upon proof of out-of-state licensure and payment of fees.

Out-of-state license accepted as pathway to journeyperson exam if based on training equal to RI requirements. Military members/spouses licensed in another state for at least one year may receive a license if requirements are substantially equivalent.

Applicant must hold a license or certificate in good standing in another state with equal or greater requirements; board must have authorized an exam waiver agreement. Applicant may also exempt the technical exam by verifying passage of a substantially equivalent exam in another state. South Carolina Commercial Contractors Business, Law and Project Management examination may still be required.
Proof that the applicant's qualifications are equal to SD licensees of the same class; payment of required fee; other state must provide for similar action.
Reciprocity is available with states that practice reciprocity with Tennessee; applicants from non-reciprocal states must apply in writing and meet board requirements.
Applicant must hold a license in another state with a reciprocity agreement, submit a proper application, and pay required fees.
License in another state with similar scope of practice, at least one year of experience under that license, and license in good standing.

Individual must hold a current and valid license in another state for at least 3 years, pass required exams, have no pending investigations or unresolved complaints, be in good standing, have no disqualifying criminal record, and pay all applicable fees.

Reciprocity requires equivalent standards and mutual recognition. Additionally, the Board shall issue a license to master and journeyman electricians licensed in good standing in another U.S. jurisdiction for at least three years, regardless of whether that jurisdiction meets reciprocity requirements.

Other state's requirements must be equal to Washington's standards. Out-of-state applicants must provide evidence of equivalent qualifications; a temporary permit may be issued while the application is pending.

The education, experience, and examination requirements in the other state must be at least equivalent to Wisconsin's requirements; applicant must submit an application, pay applicable fee, and hold a valid comparable credential from the other state.
Reciprocity available to the extent other states provide for similar action; applicant must show qualifications equal to WV licensees, pay required fee, and provide required certification.
Applicant must have obtained an out-of-state or foreign license through an examination equal to or exceeding Wyoming's examination

assignments.raw_value: "electrical administrator" means a person who is responsible for (A) installing or repairing electrical wiring, conduits, devices, fixtures, equipment, or other electrical materials for transmitting, using, or consuming electrical energy; or (B) certifying that an installation or repair described in (A) of this paragraph complies with applicable electrical codes
Any job or project in the State of Alabama wherein the electrical contractor proposes to bid, install, maintain, alter, or repair any electric wiring devices or equipment.

"Electrical work" means: (A) Installations of electric conductors and equipment within or on public and private buildings or other structures, including recreational vehicles and floating buildings, and other premises such as yards, carnivals, parking and other lots, and industrial substations; (B) Installations of conductors that connect to the supply of electricity; and (C) Installations of other outside conductors on the premises;

Specialty commercial contracting, which is engaging in the contracting business in the performance of construction work requiring special skill and involving the use of specialized construction trades or crafts other than residential contracting.

a contractor is any person who undertakes to or offers to undertake to, or purports to have the capacity to undertake to, or submits a bid to, or does himself or herself or by or through others, construct, alter, repair, add to, subtract from, improve, move, wreck or demolish any building, highway, road, parking facility, railroad, excavation or other structure, project, development or improvement
Electrical work means wiring for, installing, and repairing electrical apparatus and equipment for electric light, heat, and power.

Master electrician means a person, licensed by the Board, to plan, estimate, layout, perform or supervise the installation, erection or repair of any electrical conductor, molding, duct, raceway, conduit, machinery, apparatus, device or fixture for the purpose of lighting, heating or power in any structure.

"Electrical contractor" or "unlimited electrical contractor" means a person who conducts business in the electrical trade field and who has the experience, knowledge, and skill to install, repair, alter, add to, or design, in compliance with law, electrical wiring, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduit, or any part thereof, which generates, transmits, transforms, or utilizes electrical energy in any form, including the electrical installations and systems within plants and substations, all in compliance with applicable plans, specifications, codes, laws, and regulations.

"Electrical contracting" means the installation, maintenance, alteration, or repair of any electrical equipment, apparatus, control system, or electrical wiring device which is attached to or incorporated into any building or structure in this state but shall not include low-voltage contracting.
"Supervising electrician" means any person who has been licensed by the board as a supervising electrician to direct and supervise the performance of electrical work and to perform electrical work.

no person shall, for another, wire for or install electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment, or supervise an apprentice electrician or unclassified person, unless the person is licensed by the board as an electrical contractor, a class A master electrician, or a class B master electrician, or is licensed as a class A journeyman electrician or a class B journeyman electrician

any person who personally performs or supervises the actual physical work of installing electrical wiring or equipment to convey electric current, or apparatus to be operated by such current, or engages in planning, lay out, or design of such wiring, equipment, or apparatus, or the supervision thereof, shall for the purpose of this chapter be known as a journeyman electrician

"Electrician" means any person licensed by the department who is employed by an electrical contractor and is engaged in the construction, alteration, or repair of any electrical system used for the purpose of furnishing heat, light, or power

"Electrical contractor" means any person who undertakes to, attempts to, or submits a price or bid or offers to construct, supervise, superintend, oversee, direct, perform, or in any manner assume charge of the construction, alteration, repair, improvement, movement, demolition, putting up, tearing down, or furnishing labor together with material and equipment, or installing the same for the wiring, fixtures, or appliances for the supply of electricity to any residential, commercial, or other project, for which the project value is ten thousand dollars or more.

''Journeyman electrician'', a person qualified to do the work of installing, repairing, or maintaining wires, conduits, apparatus, devices, fixtures, or other appliances used for heat, light, power, fire warning or security system purposes.

"Provide electrical services" means to provide any service in the electrical trade. "Provide electrical services" includes installing, repairing, maintaining, erecting, or altering any electrical equipment, wiring, fixture, appliance, apparatus, raceway, conduit, or system that: (i) generates, transmits, transforms, or uses electrical energy in any form for light, heat, power, or communication; and (ii) is located within a plant, substation, or elsewhere.

"Electrical installations" means the installation, repair, alteration and maintenance of electrical conductors, fittings, devices and fixtures for heating, lighting, power purposes or heat activated fire alarms, intrusion alarms, energy management, telephone, cable and closed-circuit television, sound systems, data transmission, conduit and raceway systems and electrically supervised manual fire alarms and sprinkler systems.

Electrical wiring means all wiring, generating equipment, fixtures, appliances, devices, and appurtenances in connection with the generation, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy, in or on a building, residence, structure, or properties, regardless of whether or not the electrical wiring is energized at the time of installation.

"Electrical work" means the installing, altering, repairing, planning, or laying out of electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electrical light, heat, power, technology circuits or systems, or other purposes.

"Electrical contracting", engaging in the business of installing, erecting, or maintaining electrical wiring, fixtures, apparatus, equipment, devices, or components, regardless of voltage, that are used for generation, transmission, and utilization of electricity

Any person contracting or undertaking as prime contractor, subcontractor or sub-subcontractor of any tier to do any erection, building, construction, reconstruction, demolition, repair, maintenance or related work on any public or private project

Electrical construction means work performed by an individual, firm, or corporation in which an electrical connection is made to a supply of electricity or in which electricity is supplied to any electric equipment installation for which a permit is required by the authority having jurisdiction.

Electrical contracting shall be defined as engaging or offering to engage in the business of installing, maintaining, altering or repairing any electric work, wiring, devices, appliances or equipment.

A person may not undertake or plan to undertake with another person to plan, lay out, supervise, install, make additions, make alterations, or make repairs, in the installation of wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electric light, heat, or power or for a power limited system, unless licensed by the board.

Journeyman electrician means a person having the necessary qualifications, training, experience, and technical knowledge to wire for or install electrical wiring, apparatus, and equipment and to supervise apprentice electricians and who is licensed by the board

"Electrical installations" means the installation, repair, alteration and maintenance of electrical conductors, fittings, devices and fixtures for heating, lighting or power purposes, regardless of the voltage.

Electrical contractor means a person who engages in the business of contracting to install, erect, repair or alter electrical equipment for the generation, transmission or utilization of electrical energy

"electrical wiring" means all wiring, conductors, fixtures, devices, conduits, appliances or other equipment, including generating equipment such as solar electricity generating equipment of not over ten kilowatt capacity, used in connection with the general distribution or use of electrical energy

"License" means a license the Ohio construction industry licensing board issues to an individual as a heating, ventilating, and air conditioning contractor, refrigeration contractor, electrical contractor, plumbing contractor, or hydronics contractor.

Journeyman electrician means any person other than an electrical contractor who engages in the actual installation, alteration, repair or renovation of electrical facilities or electrical construction work unless specifically exempted by the provisions of the Electrical License Act

"Electrical installations" means the construction or installation of electrical wiring and the permanent attachment or installation of electrical products in or on any structure that is not itself an electrical product. "Electrical installation" also means the maintenance or repair of installed electrical wiring and permanently attached electrical products.

"Electrical contractor" means a corporation, firm, or person, who or that, by the employment of journeypersons, performs the work of installing, maintaining, servicing, and testing wires, conduits, apparatus, fixtures, and other appliances for carrying or using electricity for light, heat, or power purposes exclusive of low-voltage wiring for heating or refrigeration equipment for service, maintenance, and installation.

"Electrical" which includes the installation, alteration, or repair of wiring-related electrical material and equipment used in the generating, transmitting, or utilization of electrical energy less than six hundred volts, including all overhead electrical wiring on public rights-of-way for signs and street decorations and all underground electrical distribution systems of less than six hundred volts serving private properties.

"Electrical contractor," a person having the necessary qualifications, training, experience, and technical knowledge to plan, lay out, and supervise the installation and repair of electrical wiring, apparatus, and equipment for electric light, heat and power in accordance with the standard rules governing such work; and who undertakes or offers to undertake with another to plan for, lay out, supervise and install or to make additions, alterations and repairs in the installation of such work

"Limited licensed electrician" means any person or entity that performs any electrical work that has a total cost of less than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) and that is required to be registered under § 68-102-150

"Electrical work" means any labor or material used in installing, maintaining, or extending an electrical wiring system and the appurtenances, apparatus, or equipment used in connection with the use of electrical energy in, on, outside, or attached to a building, residence, structure, property, or premises.

"Electrical trade" means the performance of any electrical work involved in the installation, construction, alteration, change, repair, removal, or maintenance of facilities, buildings, or appendages or appurtenances.

"Electrical installation" means wires, fixtures, or apparatus installed in a complex structure or at the construction site of such structure for the transmission and use of commercially supplied or privately generated electrical energy.

"Electrical construction trade" includes, but is not limited to, installing or maintaining electrical wires and equipment that are used for light, heat, or power and installing and maintaining remote control, signaling, power limited, or communication circuits or systems.

"Electrical wiring" means all equipment, wiring, material, fittings, devices, appliances, fixtures, and apparatus used for the production, modification, regulation, control, distribution, utilization, or safeguarding of electrical energy for mechanical, chemical, cosmetic, heating, lighting, or similar purposes, as specified under the state electrical wiring code.

"Electrical contractor" means a person who engages in the business of contracting to install, erect, repair, or alter electrical equipment for the generation, transmission, or utilization of electrical energy.
"Installation of electric equipment" includes installing, altering and repairing the wiring of apparatus equipment and conductors subject to the National Electrical Code
